CCT Auto Trans announced Tuesday that it has acquired fellow car hauler Livingston Vehicle Transportation Services (VTS).
Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
Livingston VTS operates one of Canada’s largest vehicle-hauling networks, using its own fleet of trucks and car haulers. It has seven locations nationally and partners with Canadian National ( NYSE: CNI ) for transcontinental moves. Its customer base spans auto manufacturers to individuals.
Livingston VTS was an operating unit of Livingston International, one of Canada’s largest customs brokers.
“Livingston VTS has a very solid customer base, dedicated , long-term staff and drivers with assets in most major cities across Canada,” said Chad Doiron, CCT Auto Trans president and CEO, in a news release. “This acquisition positions CCT as the only company in Canada delivering open, enclosed and rail vehicle transport. It provides us with an asset-based, national footprint and the ability to expand in those locations with our current customers.”
Parent company CCT Group of Companies will operate Livingston VTS under CCT Vehicle Transportation Solutions . Livingston VTS employees and drivers will transition to the new operation.
“We value the contributions our VTS associates have made and are proud of the work they have done over the years to support our customers,” said Livingston CEO Robert Smith. “This is a win for both organizations, allowing VTS operations to continue to grow under the management of a company with a long and successful history in vehicle hauling while enabling Livingston to focus on its core business.”
CCT provides finished vehicle transportation with a fleet of 90 open auto carrier units and more than 80 employees, including drivers.
The announcement follows other recent deals in the car haul space.
In August, finished vehicle transportation provider Acertus announced it acquired Fisher Shipping . The same month, Proficient Auto Logistics ( NASDAQ: PAL ) acquired Hansen & Adkins for $130 million. Jack Cooper closed its doors in early 2025.
Left Lane Associates represented Livingston in the transaction.
Why it matters? This acquisition highlights a clear trend toward consolidation within the car haul sector as operators look to gain scale, expand geographies and integrate service offerings.

Meet Stargazer, a One-Off Tiny House With a Drop-Down Deck, Japanese Soaking Tub, and Murphy Bed
24 photos
Photo: Exploring Alternatives/YouTube screenshot
Many people keep clear of tiny living because they believe it implies serious trade-offs in regard to space and comfort. But what if a tiny house could offer the comfort of a conventional home, the mobility of an RV, and a slew of surprise features that maximize the use of space?
The Stargazer tiny house tries to make small-space living as comfortable and appealing as possible with multifunctional, convertible furniture, an expanding bathroom, and a rear wall that drops down to create an outdoor deck.
This clever tiny home on wheels is a one-off creation that was built as part of an experiment called The Tiny House Master Plan. The idea was to build a house completely for free, document the entire process as a show at no cost, and then give the finished home away to a lucky winner. The mastermind behind this project is Kenton Zerbin, a British Columbia-based sustainable living educator who lives in an off-grid tiny house of his own.
He aimed to create a home that was a peak example of good design, to demonstrate what can be achieved in a compact space with creativity, innovative ideas, and craftsmanship. He completed the project with help from over fifty sponsors, many volunteers, and students, all passionate about sustainable living, tiny homes , and community.
“What started as a bold experiment to build and give away a tiny house for free turned into one of the most challenging and meaningful projects I’ve ever taken on,” Kenton says.
Photo: Exploring Alternatives/YouTube screenshot In the video attached below, he explains that function took priority over appearance when designing the Stargazer. The result is a home that is not only livable but also highly efficient and ready to be used off-grid. Its base is a triple-axle gooseneck trailer from Timber Suspension Systems with a suspension system and built-in jacks on all four corners.
It measures 26 feet (7.9 meters) long at the base, with an extra 7 feet (2.1 meters) extending over the gooseneck section, bringing the total length to 33 feet (10 meters). With a width of 8.5 feet (2.6 meters), it can legally be transported on public roads without special permits.
Because it was built with the assumption that it would serve as a roving home , they designed it with lightweight materials and an aerodynamic shape. It features metal framing and aluminum siding to keep weight down, while the angled roof at the front lets air flow around it. The exterior is clad in a combination of black and natural wood-tone aluminum plank siding from FastPlank Systems, a diamond plate protects the front side, and storage compartments are integrated on both sides to hold utility equipment and other things you don’t want inside the house.
Photo: Exploring Alternatives/YouTube screenshot It’s also worth mentioning that Stargazer is designed for year-round living , with spray foam insulation all around, including underneath the trailer. It is also equipped with a heat recovery ventilation (HRV) system, which brings fresh air inside and exhausts stale air without losing heat.
Stargazer’s interior comes to roughly 280 square feet (26 square meters) and boasts a layout that puts the living area at the front, the kitchen in the middle, and the bathroom and bedroom toward the rear. What makes it highly functional is a series of innovative features that you don’t see in other tiny homes , such as an expanding bathroom with a Japanese-inspired soaker tub, a built-in deck that creates an open-air bedroom or home office, as well as transforming furniture like a Murphy bed and a convertible dinette.
The living area consists of two sofa benches and a cherrywood table operated by an electric lifting mechanism. When in raised position, the table creates a dining space for at least six people, and if you lower it and combine it with cushions, you get a large king-size bed. The whole front wall is full of storage cabinets; some hold the propane tanks and the rest are perfect for storing cushions, bedding, pillows, and more. A TV is mounted on the wall for entertainment.
Photo: Exploring Alternatives/YouTube screenshot The kitchen features long concrete countertops and incorporates a central peninsula that doubles as a bar, while the section next to the living room can serve as a desk. It functions just like a conventional kitchen in a “real” home thanks to a double-basin sink, a Dometic two-burner gas cooktop, a range hood, and an apartment-size refrigerator.
Cabinets surround the work area with much-needed storage, and large windows bring natural light inside. Kenton also added a small wood stove above the peninsula, adding both warmth and character.
A hallway leads to the private areas. Hallways are usually dead spaces in tiny homes, but Kenton didn’t want to waste any space, which is why he created a clever door system that allows the passage to become part of the bathroom. The doors basically close off the hallway, increasing the bathroom space by almost 33%.
Photo: Exploring Alternatives/YouTube screenshot The bathroom itself is fully tiled and includes a large shower stall with a cedar shower pan that lifts to reveal a Japanese soaker tub built into the floor. It’s made of lightweight concrete and offers a nice bathing experience. A compact vanity with a wall-mounted faucet and a Separett composting toilet are also included.
The bedroom at the rear is designed as a flexible space with a Murphy bed that gets out of the way when not needed and a large storage unit with cabinets. Owners can add a pivoting or flip-up desk to turn the room into a home office. One of the most surprising features, however, is the back wall, which drops down to form a built-in deck, extending the room to the outside.
The newly created opening comes with two screens - one serves as a projector screen for outdoor movie nights, while the other is a bug screen. The overhang above the deck acts as a natural awning.
Photo: Exploring Alternatives/YouTube screenshot As mentioned, the Stargazer was designed as a self-contained home , and its off-grid equipment includes solar panels, a charge controller, batteries, onboard water tanks, a composting toilet, and a small wood stove. Conventional RV hookups are also available, so the house can connect to the grid as well.
This one-of-a-kind tiny home was won by a family of four living on a farm, and they say it’s a great addition to their property.
The Stargazer project was intended to cost nothing through sponsorships and volunteer contributions, but a house like this still requires a great amount of resources. Kenton says he didn’t keep track of the team’s labor hours, but he estimates that materials alone cost between CAD $80,000 and $100,000 (USD $56,300 to $70,400), and that a professional builder would aks at least CAD $200,000 (USD $140,800) for a similar build.

Tesla sold 381,088 cars to Chinese buyers through the first nine months of 2026, down 11.9% from last year, according to CPCA data. Over the same period, Giga Shanghai’s exports more than doubled to 361,972 vehicles.
Nearly half of what Tesla builds in China now leaves China. And Beijing just announced it will cut the tax rebate on EV exports next year.
“Affordable cars must be made on same continent as customers”
When Tesla broke ground on Giga Shanghai in January 2019 , Elon Musk was clear about who the factory was for.
“Shanghai Giga will produce affordable versions of 3/Y for greater China,” Musk wrote at the time. He added that the Model S, Model X and “higher cost versions” of the Model 3 and Model Y would “still be built in US for WW market, incl China.” In another post that same week, he summed up the philosophy: “Affordable cars must be made on same continent as customers.”

That lasted about a year and a half. By late 2020, Shanghai was building right-hand-drive Model 3s for Australia and New Zealand and shipping Model 3s to Europe. Today it supplies Europe, Asia-Pacific and, since this year, Canada again under Ottawa’s new China EV import quota .
None of those customers are on the same continent as Shanghai.
Tesla’s China sales keep sliding
Here’s how Tesla’s China business looks through September, based on CPCA data:
Tesla China | Jan–Sep 2025 | Jan–Sep 2026 | Change
Retail (domestic) | 432,704 | 381,088 | -11.9%
Exports | 173,660 | 361,972 | +108%
Wholesale (total) | 606,364 | 743,060 | +22.5%
Exports as share of wholesale | 29% | 49% | +20 pts
The domestic number is the lowest first nine months Tesla has posted in China in at least four years. It’s down 17% from the 460,203 cars Tesla sold there over the same period in 2024.
Q3 was worse. Tesla’s Chinese retail sales fell 16% to 142,133 units, and July alone was down 33%. September (64,837 units, down 9.4%) was the best month of the quarter, but it was still a decline.
The whole Chinese EV market is shrinking this year, so some of this isn’t Tesla-specific. NEV retail sales in China are down 12.8% through September, according to the CPCA, after Beijing cut the purchase tax exemption in half on January 1. So Tesla is roughly tracking the market year-to-date. But in Q3, the market was down about 10% and Tesla was down 16%.
The wholesale numbers hide it
You wouldn’t know any of this from Tesla China’s headline numbers. Wholesale, which counts both domestic sales and exports, is up 22.5% this year, and July’s 93,579 units was the factory’s best July ever.
That’s all exports. Tesla has already shipped more cars out of China this year (361,972) than it did in all of 2023 (344,078), 2024 (259,548) or 2025 (226,034).
As we pointed out in our H1 analysis , Shanghai has become Tesla’s pressure valve. It can keep running near capacity even as Chinese buyers walk away, because the cars go somewhere else.
And it’s carrying the whole company. Shanghai’s wholesale volume in Q3 was 275,111 vehicles, equal to 57% of the 486,532 cars Tesla delivered worldwide . Chinese buyers accounted for just 29%.
Beijing is cutting the export rebate
On Monday, China’s Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration announced that the VAT export rebate on new energy vehicles will drop from 13% to 9% on April 1, 2027. It covers battery-electric and plug-in hybrid cars, and the rate is based on the export date on the customs declaration.
It’s part of a pattern. Beijing already eliminated the export rebate on solar panels in April, and the battery rebate was cut from 9% to 6% and goes to zero on January 1, 2027.
The mechanics are simple. Chinese exporters get the VAT they paid refunded when a product leaves the country. Whatever isn’t refunded becomes a cost. So starting in April, automakers eat an extra 4% of the export value on every EV they ship out of China.
For Tesla, that’s real money. Assuming an average export value of around ¥220,000 per Model 3 or Model Y, the cut costs about ¥8,800 ($1,235) per car. At this year’s export pace of roughly 480,000 vehicles a year, that’s around $600 million annually that Tesla either absorbs or passes on to buyers in Europe, Canada and Asia. That’s our estimate, not a Tesla figure.
Tesla isn’t alone. China exported more than 4 million NEVs in the first nine months of the year, more than double last year, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers. Every Chinese automaker that’s been using exports to offset weak demand at home gets the same bill.
But few are as exposed as Tesla, with half its Chinese production going abroad and its domestic sales falling.
There’s one more effect to watch. Since the rate depends on the customs declaration date, expect automakers, Tesla included, to cram as many exports as possible into Q4 and Q1 before the deadline. That should make Tesla China’s wholesale numbers look great for two more quarters, before the cost shows up in Q2 2027.
Electrek’s Take
Musk said Giga Shanghai would build affordable cars for China. It did, for about a year. Then it became Tesla’s export hub, and now it’s more than that: it’s the thing propping up Tesla’s China numbers and a big chunk of its global deliveries.
That shift was a reaction to falling demand. Tesla’s lineup in China is still the Model 3 and Model Y, while BYD, Xiaomi, Xpeng and a dozen others launch new models every few months at lower prices. Chinese buyers have options, and fewer of them are picking Tesla. Exports let Tesla keep the factory busy without cutting production, and the “record” wholesale did the rest.
Beijing’s rebate cut makes that model more expensive. Tesla has three options, and none of them are good. It can raise prices abroad, in markets like Europe where its sales are already weak. It can eat a margin hit of roughly $600 million a year at a time when its automotive margins are already thin. Or it can build fewer cars in Shanghai.
Berlin could take on more Model Y volume for Europe, but that doesn’t help the Model 3, Canada or Asia-Pacific.
So the question for 2027 is this: what happens to Giga Shanghai when both its home market and its export valve shrink at the same time?

WASHINGTON — Teledyne FLIR Defense has unveiled a new small counter-unmanned aerial system radar to aid forces in detection and tracking threats, the company announced today.
Dubbed Ranger R10-3DX, the c-UAS was designed to support a raft of missions such as counter-drone, force protection, airport security, border security, coastal surveillance and others, the company said.
“Small unmanned aircraft continue to present growing security challenges across military installations, airports, and other key infrastructure sites worldwide,” Rob Tarantino, senior vice president of surveillance at Teledyne FLIR Defense, said in the company’s release. “The Ranger R10-3DX gives operators an affordable, compact, and highly capable radar solution that delivers the early warning and tracking performance needed to counter evolving drone threats.”
The system uses “advanced digital beam-forming technology” and “provides continuous wide-area coverage and rapid threat detection,” the company said, all within a small system. It uses artificial intelligence for target classification, tracking multiple targets simultaneously, to distinguish between drones, planes, bird, people and vehicles while maintaining a small size.
The Ranger R10-3DX is capable of detecting micro drones as far away as three km (1.86 miles), pedestrians beyond six kilometers and vehicles at over 12 kilometers, Teledyne said. It can be outfitted for fixed-site installation or on mobile platforms, to include austere environments.

Truckload linehaul rates surged again in September while shipment counts remained in positive territory, according to a monthly report from Cass Information Systems.
Cass’ TL linehaul index, which tracks rates excluding fuel and accessorial surcharges, increased 10.1% year over year, according to Tuesday data from the payments management company. The dataset was up 0.6% from August to the highest absolute reading in four years.
The linehaul index is historically heavily weighted to contract rates but includes for-hire spot rates. September marked the 21st straight month of y/y growth (12.9% higher on a two-year-stacked comparison).
The report noted the sequential growth rate was 30 basis points below the year-to-date average. It cited a pullback in spot rates and fewer contractual bids “this time of year.”
“Even as spot rates slow with modest sequential declines, the much larger contract market is still adjusting higher.”
September 2026 | y/y | 2-year | m/m | m/m (SA)
Shipments | 1.9% | -3.6% | 2.3% | 1.4%
Expenditures | 20.4% | 23.1% | 6.7% | 4.0%
TL Linehaul Index | 10.1% | 12.9% | 0.6% | NM
Table: Cass Information Systems (SA – seasonally adjusted)
Truckload carriers on hand at investor conference last month noted they remained in a position of strength this bid season . Executives believe that the capacity exodus is growing, not slowing , and that the regulatory crackdown will likely remove thousands more unsafe operators. Management teams were also unfazed earlier this summer when the spot market entered its typical seasonal slowdown.
SONAR: Outbound Tender Rejection Index (OTRI.USA) for 2026 (blue shaded area), 2025 (yellow line), 2024 (green line) and 2023 (pink line). A proxy for truck capacity, the tender rejection index shows the number of loads being rejected by carriers. Current tender rejections show a tight truckload market. To learn more about SONAR, click here .
Werner Enterprises’ ( NASDAQ: WERN ) third-quarter guidance calls for a 10% to 13% y/y increase in rate per total mile at its one-way fleet. Earnings season starts on Thursday when J.B. Hunt Transport Services ( NASDAQ: JBHT ) reports results after the market closes.
SONAR: National Truckload Index (linehaul only – NTIL.USA) for 2026 (blue shaded area), 2025 (yellow line), 2024 (green line) and 2023 (pink line). The NTIL is based on an average of booked spot dry van loads from 250,000 lanes. The NTIL is a seven-day moving average of linehaul spot rates excluding fuel. Rates remained significantly higher on a y/y comparison in September.
SONAR: Van Contract Rate Per Mile Index ( VCRPM1.USA ) for 2026 (blue shaded area), 2025 (yellow line), 2024 (green line) and 2023 (pink line). The index shows a 7-day moving average of the initial reporting of dry van contract rates without fuel or accessorial charges.
Freight shipments recorded by Cass increased 1.9% y/y in September. The y/y increase was the second consecutive following 42 months of declines. Shipments were up 2.3% from August (1.4% higher seasonally adjusted).
All domestic transportation modes are included in the index, with TL and less-than-truckload shipments representing the bulk of the dataset. Road-to-rail conversion has weighed on the trucking-centric index in recent months as fuel prices have surged.
“With modest retail and industrial growth, and some inventory restocking as container imports surge, freight demand is recovering,” the report said. “The combination of a smaller private fleet and rising new equipment sales also supports higher for-hire volumes.”
U.S. manufacturing activity remained in positive territory for a ninth straight month during September. The Institute for Supply Management’s Manufacturing PMI registered a 54.5 reading, with the new orders dataset logging a 55.3 reading. (A reading above 50 for the index signals expansion, while one below 50 indicates contraction.)
Cass’ shipments index is forecast to increase 4% y/y in October, assuming normal seasonal patterns hold.
Cass’ expenditures index, which measures total freight spend including fuel, jumped 20.4% y/y (up 6.7% sequentially). An increase in shipments, higher freight rates and surging diesel prices drove the index higher. Diesel prices were up 68% y/y in September, 15% higher than August.
The expenditures index is expected to increase 23% y/y in October.
Data used in the indexes comes from freight bills paid by Cass ( NASDAQ: CASS ). Cass processes $37 billion in freight payables annually on behalf of customers.
Why it matters? September data from Cass highlights a continued surge in TL contract rates, with only modestly improving demand. The dataset confirms the impact strict regulatory enforcement is having on non-compliant capacity.

BYD Great Han EV prices and range
The Great Han, or “Da Han” as it’s sold in China, is BYD’s first fully electric D-segment flagship sedan under its Dynasty series.
BYD launched the luxury sedan in China on Tuesday with three variants, priced from 235,900 yuan, or about $35,000.
It’s available in single- and dual-motor powertrains. The base rear-wheel-drive (RWD) Premium model offers a CLTC range of up to 1,008 km (626 miles), while the top-spec all-wheel-drive (AWD) Flagship variant provides 880 km (546 miles).

All Great Han models also include a roof-mounted LiDAR and BYD’s God’s Eye B intelligent driver assistance system.

Breitling Is Making Super Chronomat Luxury Watches Exclusively for Aston Martin Valhalla Owners
10 photos
Photo: Aston Martin
Having enough resources to afford buying a million-dollar Aston Martin Valhalla puts one in a special class of our society. Not only in terms of wealth, but also when it comes to the love for cars and driving – after all, one really needs to be head over heels with such things, as the Valhalla has been designed to be driven rather than kept in a garage.
This special class of people also has access to perks not available to the rest of us, especially to stuff that relates directly to the design and extras that are to be fitted onto their vehicles. And they also draw the attention of other luxury brands that are after their money.
As you know, Aston Martin launched the Valhalla as its first-ever series-production, mid-engine PHEV supercar at the end of last year, with plans to make just 999 units of it. Each of them throws onto the road a combination of a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 engine and three electric motors, delivering together a maximum of 1,064 horsepower.
The Valhalla may be a series-production car, but by no means will the 999 units be all the same. Because this is the luxury world we’re talking about, buyers of this ride will have a pretty strong say in how their personal Valhalla will be specced.
And this is where Swiss watchmaker Breitling , the British carmaker’s official watch partner, comes in, ready to throw in a little extra to make Valhalla owners feel a bit more special.
The two companies announced this week that Breitling’s Super Chronomat collection of watches can be exclusively customized by each Valhalla owner to reflect not only their dreams, desires, likes, and passions, but also the hypercar they drive.
This is the first time the Swiss are opening the design process for one of their most high-profile collections, and they do this by launching a dedicated and off-the-grid configurator that can be accessed by owners.
There are two watches on the table for this: the Super Chronomat B19 44 Perpetual Calendar Chronograph and the Super Chronomat Automatic 38. The former comes with a 44 mm titanium case tied to a Rouleaux bracelet and features something its maker describes as one of the rarest combinations in the industry: an automatic perpetual calendar chronograph.
The Super Chronomat Automatic 38, on the other hand, features a 38 mm stainless-steel case and the same Rouleaux bracelet, with an automatic three-hand display taking center stage over the dial's technical pattern.
Neither Aston Martin nor Breitling said very much about the customization options available to buyers, other than the fact they can feature various colors and engravings. We also don’t know how much one costs (tens of thousands of dollars would probably be a safe bet), but, given the watches’ custom nature, that’s something for buyers alone to know.

Lockheed Martin is weighing new industry partnerships to produce urgently needed PAC-3 Patriot interceptors in Europe, an avenue that could also help fill Ukraine’s shortfalls, a company executive said.
Discussions about producing more Patriot interceptors outside the United States have picked up steam since Ukrainian leaders said over the summer they were promised by the Trump administration a license to make them in Ukraine to defend against Russian missile and drone barrages.
U.S. government officials are still expected to make a decision, which could entail the production of PAC-2 interceptors, made by Raytheon, or Lockheed’s PAC-3.
“From a PAC-3 perspective, we’re absolutely willing to talk to Ukraine,” Jason Reynolds, vice president and general manager of the company’s integrated air and missile defense division, told Defense News in an interview at the Association of the United States Army annual convention.
RELATED
Patriot interceptor deliveries to Poland will be delayed, top general says
Deliveries of some U.S. weapons systems to Poland are set to be delayed, including interceptors for the Patriot air defense system.
By Reuters
“It’s really a matter of what’s their industrial capability, what’s the parts availability, those types of things,” he continued. “It might be something like an ACE, as opposed to an MSE, that we would start with for Ukraine.”
Lockheed announced development of an ACE variant during the summer, billing it as a cheaper option against relatively simple threats — at half the cost of an MSE missile designed to go against sophisticated missiles. The new interceptor will make do with a single-pulse motor, compared with a dual-pulse of the MSE interceptor, and utilize a blast fragmentation warhead, versus the direct hit-to-kill mechanics of the MSE missile.
Reynolds cautioned that setting up interceptor missile production of whatever variant in Ukraine comes with the risk of Russian attacks on the plant.
“The first question is, ‘Can we build a factory that’s survivable in a war zone?’” he said.
That’s why the company is considering options to make them in nearby safe countries instead, and quickly ferrying them into Ukraine as they are needed.
“There is a whole number of countries that are interested in potentially producing ACE,” Reynolds said. “If we can get that started, get the supply chain started and then migrate to Ukraine as an option, that would make a lot of sense to me.”
Germany is among the countries where leaders have offered to host PAC-3 production . Raytheon, in partnership with MBDA, already makes the PAC-2 product line in the country.
For an eventual PAC-3 production, Lockheed is considering partnering with Diehl Defence, with which there is a cooperation agreement on interceptor parts in place dating from October 2025, Reynolds said.
“If we were to go forward with exploring any kind of production in Germany, we would likely do that with a company like Diehl,” he told Defense News.
A Diehl spokesperson confirmed consultations ongoing with Lockheed Martin, pointing to the October 2025 agreement. The German company has been ramping up its production capabilities at all its sites, the spokesperson added.
A new facility is in the works in Lübben, Brandenburg, which comes with requisite licensing for explosives handling because it was used by the German Democratic Republic for military equipment manufacturing.
The U.S. government has the final say about where sensitive defense products can be produced outside the United States, including Patriot air-defense equipment.
“We at Lockheed don’t have the authority to just build factories wherever we want,” Reynolds noted.

Chevy's 2027 Silverado 1500 Prefers 91-Octane Premium Gas If Optioned With Top V8 Engine
33 photos
Photo: Chevrolet / edited
Premium fuel is recommended in the redesigned Silverado 1500 with the most powerful V8 option, which also happens to be the second-largest small block from the sixth generation at 6.6 liters compared to 6.7 for the LS6 of the Corvette. Internally referred to as L78, the dual-injected truck engine is listed with 91 or greater octane by Chevrolet in the owner's manual for model year 2027.
Attached below, said manual further confirms that regular unleaded is recommended for the lesser 5.7-liter small block and the base 2.7-liter turbo. If no premium gas pump can be accessed in a timely fashion, 87 octane may be used to fuel the L78. That, however, comes with a warning for the customer. More specifically, Chevrolet says that swapping 91 for 87 may lead to reduced performance and drivability.
The manual further states that heavy knocking on the recommended grade means the engine needs to be serviced. Both 87-octane mills and the 91-octane small block carry that identical line, plus an explicit order not to feed them anything below regular unleaded. Given the direct injection system that works together with port fuel injectors, who can blame General Motors for this warning?
Dubbed L76, the 5.7-liter engine puts out a very respectable 402 horsepower as opposed to 350 for the 2.7-liter turbo inline-four. The hardest-working engine in the range, namely the 3.0-liter Duramax inline-six turbo diesel, prefers a diet of ultra-low-sulfur fuel with less than 20 percent biodiesel.
No gasser of the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and technically similar 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 accepts E85 corn brew, and ethanol content in the gasoline is capped at 15 percent by volume for all three gasoline options. The reasoning behind these recommendations is relatively straightforward.
Photo: General Motors High-output NA mills run calibrations that lean on pre-ignition resistance. Putting in a lower octane, the knock sensors pull timing, thus resulting in reduced performance and drivability. General Motors hasn't explained in the owner's manual how much power and torque said 6.6-liter small block delivers on 87, though said curiosity will be answered by the dyno in the near future.
The 6.6 carrying this recommendation is hardly a surprise when you realize that the 6.2 it replaces also requires 91 octane. Looking at the bigger picture, calibrating the engine for premium dinosaur juice also helped General Motors create the segment's most powerful naturally aspirated V8 engine. In optimal conditions, it delivers 481 horsepower and 501 pound-feet (679 Newton-meters).
The Silverado ZR2 and High Country both get the 6.6-liter powertrain, and by extension, said lump can also be found in the Sierra AT4X and Denali. Per a different section of the owner's manual, the L78 is the only engine option that comes with a 34.0-gallon tank (128.7 liters) by default. Said extended-range fuel tank is optional for the L76 small block and LZ0 turbo diesel.
According to the manual, the eighth VIN character identifies the engine on any 2027 model year half-ton pickup. E stands for the 2.7, while M designates the 5.7. Upping the ante to 6.6 liters gets you N as the eighth character of the vehicle identification number, while 8 designates the Duramax.
On that note, Duramax customers will have to pony up a handful of dollars for GM dexos 1 Gen 3 engine oil with a viscosity grade of 0W-20. All gassers take 0W-30 engine oil, also GM dexos 1 Gen 3. Including the filter, engine oil capacities range from 6.0 quarts (5.7 liters) for the L4B inline-four base mill to 8.0 quarts (7.6 liters) for the L76, L78, and LZ0.

While innovative medicine supported Johnson & Johnson’s “in line” earnings for the third quarter of 2026, investors were disappointed to see older medicines carrying the bag.
Johnson & Johnson’s shares slipped about 4% on third quarter earnings, as underperformance for the healthcare giant’s medtech unit outweighed decent performance for the innovative medicines segment.
J&J reported just 2.5% year-on-year growth for its medtech segment, falling 2% below consensus expectations at $8.64 billion for the third quarter. Meanwhile, the innovative medicines group grew about 8% compared to Q3 2025 to $16.76 billion. The company reported overall Q3 revenue of $25.4 billion, which landed about 4% above consensus expectations thanks to lower costs and tax expenses, Leerink Partners said in a Tuesday morning note.
The medtech results put executives on their back foot and pushed the shares down to about $253 apiece as the markets opened. CFO Joseph Wolk admitted the medtech results were disappointing but pledged to right the ship there through internal investments.
That left the therapeutics division holding the bag for J&J this quarter. Immunology blockbuster Tremfya was the standout with a 68% year over year increase in sales for just under $2.4 billion in worldwide sales for the quarter, according to analysts. Older medicines like Stelara and Simponi also contributed. J&J’s top-selling product was the blood cancer therapy Darzalex, which grew 15% since Q3 last year for $4.24 billion worldwide.
Guggenheim declared J&J’s overall results “generally in line,” but noted some pieces that were “a little disappointing.” Investors would have preferred to see more contribution from other newer medicines in J&J’s portfolio. Stelara was first approved in 2009 while Tremfya earned its first FDA nod in 2017.
Analysts pushed for details during the earnings call on the pharma’s fresher assets, such as the multiple myeloma medicine Tecvayli, which was first approved in 2022 and cleared for second-line treatment this past March. The drug brought in $312 million worldwide this quarter, compared to $177 million in Q3 last year, marking growth of 77%. Ryan Koors, VP, investor relations, attributed this climb to the new indication and earlier lines of treatment.

“Our multiple myeloma portfolio and pipeline are unmatched,” CEO Joaquin Duato declared on the call. About 80% of patients are receiving one of J&J’s products, which also includes Darzalex, during their treatment, the CEO noted.
Elsewhere, Wolk said that Icotyde, which was approved in March for plaque psoriasis, is “off to a strong start.” Specific results were not shared, but J&J has set expectations for sales of $10 billion for the Protagonist Therapeutics –partnered asset.
“We do foresee Icotyde to be one of our biggest assets in innovative medicine, and it is off to an incredibly great start,” echoed Tom Cavanaugh, executive VP and worldwide chairman of Innovative Medicine. About 20,000 patients have initiated therapy with about 9,000 prescribers already. This is “tracking better than most/all launches in psoriatic diseases,” he added.
To help build the pipeline, J&J has executed a few deals over the past year. The most recent, the acquisition of Firefly Bio and a licensing deal with Sail Biomedicines, closed in the third quarter. Each was worth about $1 billion and together the deals resulted in an impairment charge of $339 million.
J&J also finally settled decades-long litigation over its talc products, which added a further $5.52 billion in charges. Because of these charges, earnings per share dropped to about 9 cents, a 95% decline from the same period a year ago when EPS was $2.12. Oh, hello there. Finally some "depreciation" as far as the all-new Corvette ZR1X is concerned. This Red Mist example here just sold at auction for $315,000 with 1,200 miles on the clock. The original MSRP was $256,325.
The seller still made a nice profit, though. But what I’d like to focus on is the fact that this is by far the cheapest used ZR1X I’ve seen since people started flipping them. One could almost claim this is a steal at only $60,000 over MSRP – at least by late 2026 standards. I’m guessing that 12 months from now prices will go down considerably, especially as miles get added on.
My only bone to pick with this car is that there have been some reported reliability issues, and that’s not what you want to hear when you’re already paying way over MSRP on something that’s had its warranty voided.
To me, the ZR1X is something you buy if you’re frequently visiting the drag strip. Otherwise, you’ll simply be better off with the “regular” ZR1, which is plenty powerful and fast for 99.9% of car enthusiasts out there. I mean, look – in everyday traffic, even the Grand Sport X should perfectly replicate the ZR1X experience. And if all you want is a fast C8, just get a used Z06.
Anyway, aside from its Red Mist Metallic Tintcoat exterior, this ZR1X comes with a carbon-fiber rear wing, carbon fiber dive planes, Carbon Flash Metallic-painted side mirrors, LED headlights, a carbon-fiber split rear window, quad black-finished exhaust tips, plus a set of carbon fiber 20” and 21” wheels rocking Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 rubber and carbon-ceramic brakes. The wheels alone were a $14,000 option.
This also has the ZTK Performance suspension and a front-axle lift system with memory settings.
Meanwhile, interior highlights include the power-adjustable Competition Sport bucket seats in Natural leather, keyless entry, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, tan seat belts, a performance data and video recorder, front and rear cameras, a Bose Performance Series sound system, a head-up display, heated steering wheel, and plenty more.
Photo: Bring a Trailer The C8, generally speaking, is about as tech-laden a supercar as you can get. That’s what makes it such an amazing value proposition. Well, that and the performance across the entire range. Not to mention the price tag.
Speaking of performance, it all comes down to the twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter LT7 V8 , working alongside an electric motor and a 1.9-kWh liquid-cooled lithium-ion battery pack. The combined output is a monster 1,250 horsepower and 973 lb-ft (1,320 Nm) of torque. That’s enough to get you from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in under 2 seconds, and if you’re lucky, you might get close to putting up an 8.67-second quarter mile time.

Panellists at the Warsaw Security Forum discussion European military plans (Bartosz Głowacki)
WARSAW — Poland’s national defense minister is calling on Europe to develop an “enduring, predictable” alliance with the US, encompassing information exchange, military capabilities and defense industry collaboration.
“I believe that within the ‘NATO 3.0’ strategy, it is worth emphasizing a strategy for the defense industry,” Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz told the Warsaw Security Conference on Monday. “Relocating production lines and maintenance facilities to Europe, for instance, for Patriot missiles and systems, is crucial for the independence of both the United States and Europe.”
The comments arrived on the same day that Polish army operational commander Gen. Ireneusz Nowak noted at the event that Patriot deliveries are set to be held up . “At this point it looks like we are going to be affected as well,” he said. “That’s very visible in the area of PAC-3 MSE Patriot missiles, they’re going to be delayed for sure .”
Ukraine has called on European partners to supply it with additional Patriot missiles to fend off Russian attacks. Kosiniak-Kamysz said the current situation in Ukraine shows how dangerous a breakdown in supply chains would be in a crisis scenario, so Europe must do everything to be strong and independent enough to take action toward greater reindustrialization.
Additionally, he warned that the European Union has been grappling with the issue of military mobility for years, and “yet, there are still no decisions in place to allow for the free movement of our troops without requiring the consent of individual regions.”
The matter needs to be resolved as soon as possible, he stressed, through the adoption of sound legislation. “It should be automatic: if someone calls for help, they want those troops to reach them, and everyone else should provide support,” he explained.
From a big picture perspective, Europe cannot wait until 2035 to become strong, said Kosiniak-Kamysz, as he argued that NATO’s 5 percent GDP defense spending pledge should be brought forward to 2030.
Kosiniak-Kamysz said Europe must make its defense industry supply chains independent, and this is a task that needs to be addressed as a matter of urgency, because “we cannot rule out equipment from outside the European Union if it is critically needed.”
In his view, it stands to reason that collaboration with the US on items like low-cost, long-range precision strike capabilities, drones and anti-drone systems, as well as artificial intelligence, could prove worthwhile.
“So let us not rule out the possibility of creating Polish-US or European-US joint ventures, that could also tap into [SAFE] European funds,” he said. Of the €44 billion ($49 billion) from the SAFE program, nearly one-third went to Poland, and two-thirds of that amount has already been allocated to the Polish defense industry.
At a strategic level, he also declared that Poland is stronger with Washington’s backing.
“The more American troops there are in Poland, and if we have a permanent base and a lasting American military presence, the better equipped we are to shoulder responsibility for NATO’s eastern flank,” he said.
Kosiniak-Kamysz said also Warsaw will be ready for full-scale deterrence, thanks to investments in the defense industry, military mobility, transatlantic cooperation, relocating production to Europe, and joint investments in critical defense capabilities.
Speaking alongside Kosiniak-Kamysz, Minister of National Defence of Lithuania Robertas Kaunas said in the case of a Russian attack against Lithuania, it might be two weeks before US, Polish, German, British troops could arrive and reach the Soviet border to Lithuania. He echoed Kosiniak-Kamysz words, saying his country is investing in a national division, and an anti-drone air defense system, combining all different types of sensors, under a single ecosystem, backed by artificial intelligence.
Elsewhere, NATO Deputy Secretary General Radmila Shekerinska said that different things required to implement the alliance’s newly unveiled “ theory of victory ,” includes logistics, procurement and intelligence. “NATO is able to defend us. … But in order for all of us to keep this strategic advantage that we have [to] invest, create the capabilities, apply them, employ them, train the troops,” she said.
Shekerinska said NATO needs to speed up procurement procedures “to prepare [a] completely new approach in what is the capability, and how to make sure that NATO will have them when it will be needed.”
Rounding off panelist contributions, Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, Poland’s Secretary of State for Defense, said she hopes the moment has come for the US government and US companies to finally agree on co-production in Europe, as US warehouses are empty. According to her, Warsaw is open to other countries, setting up shop in Poland for maintenance, logistics or production.
“If there’s any foreign company trying to sell something to us, we are not only looking on the quality and price, we give four extra conditions: the maintenance center, co-production, local suppliers or at least investing in education here,” Sobkowiak-Czarnecka stressed. She added that the issue of standing up local maintenance centers is one the Polish government is trying to resolve with from Washington.
“We are open for co-production, we are open … [to] companies from different parts of the world, but the condition is you have to work with our industry,” she concluded.

CSX Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer Mike Cory is retiring, ending a tenure that began when he came out of retirement to join the railroad in September 2023.
Cory will work with the leadership team to ensure a smooth transition, the company said, and will provide transition services through May 8, 2027.

Casey Albright, senior vice president of Network Operations and Service Design, who has nearly 30 years at CSX.
Angel credited Cory with helping drive safety and productivity to record levels while developing a strong bench of operations leaders.
“Mike has dedicated his career to the railroad industry and has made significant contributions to CSX, our customers, and our employees,” Angel said in the company’s announcement.
Cory previously served as executive vice president and COO at CN (NYSE: CNI ), retiring from that railroad in 2019 before joining CSX four years later.

All-New Buick LaCrosse Sedan Breaks Cover in China and This Is What America Is Missing
10 photos
Photo: Buick
The 2027 Buick LaCrosse has officially launched in China. While the exterior design retains the familiar lines, the executive sedan hides completely new electrical architecture, a radically overhauled cabin layout, and sits on a highly advanced platform. The Buick LaCrosse remains exclusively manufactured in China for the Chinese market.
The exterior design has evolved with only minor changes from the fourth generation. The model now gets a broader, low-mounted front grille, updated bumper styling, sleek hidden exhaust tips, and sharper front and rear lamps that make it look wider, without altering its classic silhouette.
In the meantime, the proportions have remained unchanged, which means that the all-new Buick LaCrosse still measures 196.9 inches (5,003 millimeters) in length and sits on a wheelbase of 114.3 inches (2,905 millimeters)
However, the architecture underneath is completely new. The 2027 Buick LaCrosse has migrated onto SAIC-GM's next-generation platform, which made its debut back in 2025 with the Electra sub-brand's electrified vehicle lineup.
Photo: Buick However, the platform has been heavily adapted to house internal combustion engines while supporting advanced digital technology. The cabin is where the new generation marks its biggest shift. Buick has stripped out the previous layout to make room for over 50 premium upgrades, focused on luxury, comfort, and technology.
The 2027 LaCrosse gets a whole new massive floating center infotainment screen, alongside a digital instrument cluster, running on Qualcomm Snapdragon 8155 architecture for lightning-fast voice control responses of under 0.3 seconds and cloud connectivity. The new setup replaces the older curved screen layout.
The steering wheel, center console, and seating have been entirely redesigned. Now the premium seats feature multi-density 3D foam with extended thigh support. Upper trims pack active multi-stage ventilation and heating, along with six-point pneumatic massage functions in all four seats.
The powertrain is carried over unchanged. The 2027 Buick LaCrosse is powered by the eighth-generation Ecotec 2.0-liter turbocharged inline-four, which produces 233 horsepower (237 metric horsepower) and 258 pound-feet (350 Newton meters) of torque for a run from 0 to 60 mph in 7.2 seconds and a top speed of 143 mph (230 kph). A nine-speed automatic transmission puts the power down through the front wheels.
Photo: Buick A Level 2+ e-Cruise suite drives 14 active assistance systems, with capabilities for lane centering, full-speed adaptive cruise control, traffic jam assist, forward collision warning, and automated parking.
Buick sells the LaCrosse in two distinct trims. The LaCrosse Smart Edition starts at 149,900 yuan, which translates to roughly $22,500, and the Supreme Edition, which is a 169,900-yuan ($25,500) deal.
The all-new 2027 LaCrosse has already started rolling out to Buick's dealership network across China. There are currently no plans to reintroduce the LaCrosse to North America, where Buick has transitioned to an all- SUV brand lineup. The sedan was retired from the U.S. market after the 2019 model year.

This Almost New 2020 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 Is for Sale, Can You Guess the Price?
9 photos
Photo: VanguardMotorSales
The S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 may not have an eponymous successor, which is why some believe that the company might be prepping an ultra-hot version of the S650, but let’s not forget that the Dark Horse SC exists.
As you likely know by now, the latter model takes less than three seconds to zip from zero to sixty miles per hour (0 to 97 kph), and features a 5.2-liter supercharged V8 under the hood. The mill is officially good for 795 bhp (806 ps/593 kW) and 660 pound-feet (895 Nm) of torque, and everything is channeled to the rear wheels (what else?) through a dual-clutch seven-speed Tremec automatic transmission.
How does it compare to the S550-based Ford Mustang Shelby GT500? Well, the power boost is not jaw dropping, as there is a difference of 35 hp (36 ps/26 kW ) and 33 pound-feet (45 Nm) of torque between the two, with the balance tilting in favor of the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC (SC stands for SuperCharged). That’s because the GT500 has 760 hp (771 ps/567 kW) to play with in total, and 627 lb-ft (847 Nm) of torque from its 5.2-liter supercharged V8 engine.
Mind you, while the gap is not that significant, the performance is, or the straight-line acceleration, for that matter, which takes a little over three seconds in the Ford Mustang Shelby GT500. This model will complete the standing quarter mile in 10.7 seconds, and guess what? According to third-party estimates, that is actually one-tenth of a second faster than the Mustang Dark Horse SC. And that’s a battle worth watching.
Photo: VanguardMotorSales However, we are not here to discuss the differences and similarities between the S550-based Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 and its new-age successor, the S650 Mustang Dark Horse SC, but to put the spotlight on the GT500 pictured above. And that’s what we are doing now, because we found this example looking for a new home in the United States of America, and it is definitely worth checking out, especially if you are into this thing.
There are many reasons to love this particular pony car, and if the 760 brake horsepower available via the loud pedal is not enough to convince you, then the mileage should. That’s because this ride is said to have a mere 1,320 miles (2,125 km) under its belt, which means that it is pretty much brand new. And it likely retains that new-car smell, too. On top of that, it boasts the Carbon Fiber Track Pack, which is said to have been an $18,500 option back in the day.
As a result, it comes with the usual wheels made of the lightweight material, which measure 20 inches in diameter, and were shod in Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires. The carbon fiber rear wing is also part of this bundle, just like the rear-seat delete. Thus, you are looking at a veritable two-seater. The stopping power is provided by the Brembo brakes on all four corners, with ventilated rotors. And this ride features additional other goodies.
The listing also mentions stuff such as the 12-inch touchscreen infotainment system, a Bang & Olufsen premium sound system, a dual-zone climate control system, an Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel with paddle shifters, Recaro bucket seats wrapped in black Alcantara and white leather upholstery, dual illuminated vanity mirrors, and a few other bits and bobs, including the blind-spot assist.
Photo: VanguardMotorSales As the vendor says, this machine “ would make a great addition to any garage or collection, ” and who are we to say otherwise? After all, this is a great muscle car developed to take on those pesky two-door Dodge Hellcats back in the day, and it remains a fantastic daily that feels right at home at the drag strip.
Mind you, one definitely needs some deep pockets if they want to spruce up their life with a cool S550-based Ford Mustang Shelby GT500. That is because this thing can command upward of $160,000, depending on the model year, mileage, configuration, and overall condition. An earlier model year with quite a few miles under its belt can fetch roughly $100,000 in today’s used car market, and some examples have dropped below the $100K mark all the way to the $80k one, though they’re not exactly in pristine condition, to no one’s surprise.
Now that you know that the pictured Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 is a 2020 model year, as mentioned in the title, that it features the sought-after Carbon Fiber Track Pack, and that it has been kept away from the road for the most part, as it barely has any miles under its belt, how much do you think that this example costs? Unless you said $134,900, then you are wrong, as that was the asking price at the time of writing. The muscle car in question is advertised by Vanguard Motor Sales, and you can access the ad here .

The US has passed 80,000 public EV fast-charging ports, and new charging stops are getting bigger and packing more power. That’s good news for drivers looking for an open stall. The price story is more mixed: Most networks are holding steady, but Tesla Supercharger costs have gone up.
EV charging data platform Paren’s Q3 2026 State of the US Fast EV Charging Industry report finds that operators added 4,106 fast-charging ports at 664 stations from July through September. That brings the US total to 80,964 ports across 14,614 locations.
The rollout slowed compared to Q2, when 4,618 ports opened. Through September, operators added about 9% fewer ports and opened about 20% fewer stations than in the same period last year.
But the stations that are opening have more places to plug in. New non-Tesla sites averaged five ports, up from 4.1 a year earlier. Locations with just one or two ports made up less than a third of new non-Tesla stops, down from nearly half.

For drivers, a bigger site means more chances to grab a charger when they arrive.
IONNA and Walmart pick up speed
Tesla still added more ports than any other network: 1,287 during Q3, plus another 124 through its Supercharger for Business program.
IONNA took second place with 378 ports, more than double its Q2 additions. Walmart came in third with 344.
Much of IONNA’s jump came from converting former Circle K charging locations, including 44 stations during the quarter. There’s a counting detail to note here: Paren treats replacement chargers as new infrastructure when another operator takes over and replaces the equipment.
Tesla’s new stations averaged 13.1 ports. It opened 11 locations with at least 24 stalls, the largest of which was a 48-stall site in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.
And the new equipment is getting more powerful. Across all networks, 73% of new ports were rated at least 250 kilowatts (kW), up from 60% a year earlier. Outside Tesla’s network, ports rated at 400 kW or more accounted for 35% of additions, compared with just 10% a year ago.
More chargers, more charging
Drivers are putting the growing network to use. Paren tracked 50.4 million fast-charging sessions in Q3, up 26% year over year. July set a monthly record with 17.6 million sessions.
National utilization barely moved, reaching 15.9%, compared with 15.8% in Q2. That’s the share of monitored time a port spends charging a vehicle, including unsuccessful attempts.
That national average hides some big differences. Ports in the 30 largest charging markets averaged 21.1% utilization, compared with 11% elsewhere. Los Angeles led those metros at 31.8% – twice the national average.
Reliability held steady, too, with a national score of 93.9. Paren’s index accounts for successful sessions, retries, failed attempts, and downtime, so it isn’t simply a charger uptime percentage.
Fifty of the 52 states and territories assessed scored at least 90, up from 46 a year earlier. Only Oklahoma and Vermont remained below that mark.
Tesla charging gets pricier
Drivers who use Superchargers may have noticed a bigger dent in their wallets.
In Q3, the national average fast-charging price reached 54 cents per kilowatt-hour, up 2.7% year over year. Paren attributes that increase to Tesla.
Tesla’s average non-member Supercharger price rose 15% over the year to 56.9 cents per kWh. Its member price increased 9% to 39.6 cents.
Meanwhile, the average across non-Tesla networks stayed near 53.3 cents per kWh for the fifth consecutive quarter.
When you plug in can make a difference, too. At stations with time-of-use pricing, average peak rates reached 63.7 cents per kWh, while off-peak rates held at 43.8 cents. That’s nearly a 20-cent gap for the same amount of electricity.
Where the next chargers go also matters. Urban markets received 90% of Q3’s new stations, while rural markets got 68 of the 664 additions. Larger charging stops are welcome, but drivers beyond those urban areas still need more places to stop.

A 74-year-old truck driver from Reno, Nevada, died after his tractor-trailer left Interstate 84 and overturned east of Boise, Idaho, early Monday.
The single-vehicle crash occurred at approximately 3:08 a.m. Oct. 12 near milepost 62 in Ada County, along the eastbound lanes of I-84, according to Idaho State Police.
Authorities said the driver was operating a 2024 International semi-truck pulling a trailer when the vehicle left the roadway, traveled along an embankment for a short distance and overturned.
The driver was transported by ground ambulance to a local hospital, where he later died from his injuries.
Authorities said the driver was not wearing a seat belt at the time of the crash.
The driver’s identity had not been released in the initial police report.
The crash blocked the right eastbound lane of I-84 for approximately three hours while emergency crews responded and investigators examined the scene.
Authorities have not disclosed what caused the truck to leave the roadway. The incident remains under investigation.
Interstate 84 is a major east-west freight corridor connecting Idaho with Oregon and Utah, serving commercial trucking operations throughout the Pacific Northwest and Intermountain West.
Fatal truck crashes remain a national safety concern
Federal crash data show thousands of fatal crashes involving large commercial trucks each year, although complete figures for January through September 2026 are not yet available.
The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration ’s preliminary Motor Carrier Management Information System data, updated Aug. 28, recorded 1,607 fatal crashes involving large trucks nationwide in 2026, resulting in 1,768 deaths.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration reported that 5,340 people died in crashes involving large trucks in 2024, down 2.5% from 2023. About 70% of those killed were occupants of other vehicles.
In Idaho, preliminary figures released Sept. 11 by the Idaho Transportation Department showed 150 traffic deaths statewide in 2026, compared with 174 during the corresponding period in 2025. Those totals include all vehicle types, not just commercial trucks.
The department identified failure to wear a seat belt, failure to maintain a lane, impairment, inattention and speeding among the leading contributing circumstances in fatal crashes statewide.
Investigators in Idaho have not determined whether any of those factors, other than the driver’s reported lack of a seat belt, played a role in Monday’s crash.

The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500's Midgrade Trim Level Gets Split Into LT for 2WD and Z71 for 4WD
39 photos
Photo: Chevrolet
Half-ton pickup trim ladders used to be honest math a long time ago. Paying more resulted in getting more, and the badge told you from its name alone where you stood. Chevrolet made that game a little harder on the 2027 model year Silverado 1500, for the midrange Silverado grade answers to two names.
One drivetrain checkbox decides between them. Ordering two-wheel drive sees the Chevrolet brand's online configurator list it as the LT. Ticking the four-wheel-drive box on the same grade, however, turns it into the Z71. Chevrolet's built-in model comparison tool has made peace with this confusing arrangement already, labeling the trim Silverado (LT/Z71) at the moment of reporting.
This implies the Z71 package comes by default with four-wheel drive, and you are perfectly correct in this regard. Backing up to June 2026, when the Chevy division of General Motors unwrapped the next-gen truck, the plan looked much simpler. The media release from back then listed seven trims for the US market, including a brand-new middle grade called Silverado .
Chevrolet described it as being the previous LT in said press release, leaving many among us to read that as a death notice for the LT. After all, the RST and LTZ really did leave us. The Z71, on the other hand, is better known as an option package rather than a trim level.
Chevrolet welded the options in question to the grade for 2027, including off-road suspension, skid plates, and hill descent control for good measure. As opposed to the 2026 and earlier LT, the 2027 model does not offer a four-wheel-drive specification.
Photo: Chevrolet The most affordable Silverado 1500 presently configurable is the WT regular cab with the standard bed at $41,395. Stepping up to the LT means double cab and the standard bed at the very least, pushing the advertised price to $50,695 per the configurator. The Z71 with the double cab and standard bed, meanwhile, is $54,295 from the outset.
Both are listed with the enhanced TurboMax inline-four as the base engine, albeit with late availability, whereas the 5.7-liter small block has no such restrictions. The 2.7-liter turbo I4 develops 350 horsepower and 455 pound-feet (617 Newton-meters), and ships exclusively with a 10-speed automatic instead of the previous 8-speed transmission.
Displacing nearly 350 cubes, the 5.7 is a gen-six small block with 402 horsepower and 428 pound-feet (580 Newton-meters) at its disposal. Beyond these mills, prospective customers of the 2027 model year Silverado 1500 are further presented with the carryover 3.0-liter Duramax inline-six turbo diesel and a larger 6.6-liter small block.
Weirdly enough, the ZR2 off-road specification comes with the Duramax standard and the 6.6 if you prefer gasoline. The big eighter makes 481 horsepower and 501 pound-feet (679 Newton-meters), prompting General Motors to call it the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 in the segment.
The 5.7 and 6.6 small blocks replace the older 5.3 and 6.2 units, which rely on direct injection alone compared to dual injection for the gen-six engines. Oh, and by the way, Canada skipped the identity crisis altogether because the Silverado grade only comes with four-wheel drive there. As a result, the Z71 is the only midranger available in Canada.

Tesla Model 3 (Source: Tesla)
Tesla has stopped taking orders for the Model 3 Premium in Canada, the Shanghai-built trim that brought the electric sedan down to $39,490 CAD. The automaker says it has used up its import quota for Chinese-made EVs and doesn’t expect to reopen orders until March 2027.
But the Canadian government’s own tracker tells a different story: 33,069 of the 49,000 permits for China-made EVs in the current quota year are still available.
“Tesla’s import quota”
The change shows up in Tesla’s Canadian configurator. Both Model 3 Premium versions, RWD and AWD, are gone from the order page. The only Model 3 you can order in Canada right now is the Performance AWD, listed at $936 per month in financing.
Tesla explains the pause with a short message on its site: “Model 3 Premium orders paused after high demand exhausted Tesla’s import quota. Ordering resumes if Govt of Canada issues more quota, expected March 2027.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Canada’s quota runs on a March-to-February year, so March 1, 2027, is when a fresh 49,000 permits become available.
The Model 3 Premium RWD has been a hit since Tesla launched it in Canada at a record-low $39,490 in May . That’s roughly the price of a base Camry. Before it arrived, the cheapest Model 3 you could order in Canada was the $79,990 Long Range AWD, built in Fremont and hit by Canada’s 25% counter-tariff on US-made vehicles. Tesla shipped its remaining US-built Model 3 inventory out of Canada back in March to make room.
Ottawa’s numbers don’t show an exhausted quota
When Canada cut its tariff on Chinese EVs from 100% to 6.1% in January , it set a single national cap of 49,000 vehicles per year, split into two six-month periods. Global Affairs Canada’s notice for the current period says permits are issued “on a first-come, first-served (FCFS) basis” to automakers or their Canadian agents. There’s no per-manufacturer limit in it.
According to the Export and Import Controls tracker, updated October 9, only 15,931 permits have been used since March 1. That leaves 33,069, or 67% of the year’s quota, sitting unused. The current period alone started with 33,397 permits: the base 24,500 plus 8,897 left over from the first six months.
And the monthly breakdown shows when things stopped. Imports of electric cars valued at or under $35,000 (the customs bucket a $39,490 Model 3 RWD would fall into, since the threshold applies to import value, not sticker price) went from 465 in June to 4,743 in July and 2,597 in August. That ramp lines up with Model 3 Premium deliveries. Then September came in at just seven vehicles, and October was at zero as of the latest update.
So Tesla went from importing thousands of cheap Chinese-built cars a month to nearly none, while two-thirds of the quota stayed on the table.
The likely explanation
There’s one line in Global Affairs Canada’s notice that could explain it. The department says it will monitor permit applications “for the purpose of providing equitable access to the quota to eligible applicants,” which “could include setting aside a portion of the available quota for the use of OEMs, including new entrants.”
In plain terms, Ottawa gave itself room to stop one company from eating the whole thing. And Tesla is the obvious candidate. It had a head start because its Shanghai-built cars were already in Transport Canada’s certification database in March, while BYD and Geely are still setting up their Canadian dealer networks.
Tesla’s wording, “Tesla’s import quota,” points the same way. If permits were still open first-come, first-served, Tesla could simply keep applying. Global Affairs Canada hasn’t published any company-specific allocation, so the details of what Tesla was given, and when, aren’t public.
The other possibility is that Tesla’s order backlog is big enough that it already covers every permit it expects to get before February. Either way, Canadians who want a $39,490 Model 3 are now waiting until next spring at the earliest.
Electrek’s Take
The demand part of Tesla’s message is real. A Model 3 at $39,490 CAD is the best EV deal in Canada, full stop, and Canadians bought it in big numbers despite the anger at Elon Musk that’s still very visible here. That says a lot about how much price matters.

People can argue about which one they would rather own, but it's personal preference.

But “exhausted Tesla’s import quota” is doing a lot of work in that sentence. Canada’s official tracker shows two-thirds of the quota unused. If Ottawa quietly capped Tesla to keep room for BYD, Geely and others, we think that’s a defensible policy choice. The whole point of opening the door to Chinese EVs was more competition and lower prices, not a Tesla monopoly on the cheap import lane. If that’s what happened, though, the government should say so and publish the allocations. Automakers, dealers and buyers are all making decisions in the dark right now.
The bigger issue is the 49,000 cap itself. Canada sells roughly 1.9 million new vehicles a year. One affordable sedan from one automaker was enough to max out whatever share Tesla was allowed in about four months of deliveries. That’s a sign the quota is too small, not that demand is too big.
The quota is supposed to be reviewed, and the deal already calls for it to grow to 70,000 by 2030. After this, will Ottawa move faster than that?

Tesla Expected To Launch IFTTT-Style Automations in North America and Europe With the Holiday Update
12 photos
Photo: Maciej Wilczy?ski and Micha? Gapi?ski via X.com
In January, Tesla introduced automations in China, allowing owners to set "If This, Then That" (IFTTT) routines. Now, the carmaker is ready to expand the feature in Western markets, most probably with this winter's Holiday Update. The software already has the necessary changes for the automations to run, as revealed in recent social media posts.
Anyone with a smart home is familiar with automations, although the feature has also been popular among smartphone users for a long time. Apps like IFTTT (short for If This, Then That) have been used for years to automate tasks, and Apple has offered a Shortcuts app doing pretty much the same thing.
It was only a matter of time before Tesla would provide a similar functionality. As with many other new functions, this was first offered to customers in China with the 2025.45 32.1 update . Much like Apple, Tesla offered this via a dedicated app, aptly called "Automation." At the time, I speculated that the feature would also be offered in Western markets soon.
As predicted, Tesla is now preparing to roll out the Automation app outside China. The feature has been discovered in the Tesla software, and it appears to be a translation of the Chinese app. The discovery has been made by Maciej Wilczyński and Michał Gapiński, two Polish developers working on a joint project related to Tesla. Gapiński is best known to the Tesla community for the Tesla Android Project.
Wilczyński appreciated the Automation app as "fully polished," albeit still hidden under a feature flag, waiting to be unlocked. The developers were able to do this on their personal Teslas, and they shared videos showing how it works. The rest of Tesla owners will likely get the app with the upcoming Holiday Update , sometime in December.
The Automation app uses a typical "If This, Then That" logic, which should be familiar to anyone who used the Apple Shortcuts app on their iPhone or Tasker on an Android phone. Wilczyński's video shows how simple it is to create an automation. You just need to choose an action, a trigger, and a condition (or more) from a list of available options.
Gapiński, for instance, used the Automation app to remind his wife to use FSD (now renamed Tesla Assisted Driving in Europe) every time she fastens her seatbelt, but there really are countless possibilities. For instance, owners could set location-based reminders, time-of-day automations, and other alerts and actions based on the driver's presence or vehicle state.
Eventually, people will be able to design their own automations, adopt the ones designed by others, or choose from a marketplace. There are some limits to what the app can do, and the most important is that the screen must be active. This excludes automations running in the background while the car is parked with no one inside. Apparently, automation can't be triggered when Tesla's driver assistance features (Autopilot or TAD/ FSD ) are active, either. 1971 Dodge Demon Looks Stunning in High-Impact Butterscotch, Packs the Best Engine
10 photos
Photo: Gause Garage/YouTube
In 2018, Dodge shocked the world with the Challenger SRT Demon , a drag-ready muscle car with an 840-horsepower engine. In 2023, the company took it up a notch with the Demon 170, rated at an incredible 1,025 horsepower. But the modern Challenger wasn't the first Mopar to sport the Demon badge.
The name actually goes back to 1971, when Dodge applied it on a version of the Dart. Introduced in 1960 as a full-size car, the Dart became an intermediate in 1962. It was downsized once more to compact dimensions in 1963, retaining its market position through 1976.
The Dart was redesigned for the fourth and final generation in 1967. Much like its corporate twin, the Plymouth Valiant, the Dart was offered in two-door sedan, four-door sedan, two-door hardtop, and two-door convertible body styles. The Demon arrived when Dodge decided to introduce a two-door fastback similar to the Plymouth Duster.
The coupe was initially supposed to be named the Beaver, but Chrysler's marketing department scrapped the name when it learned that "beaver" was CB slang for a part of the female anatomy. Instead, Dodge went with the Dart Demon. It was advertised as a performance model, and a Demon 340 variant was added to replace the Swinger 340.
The Demon was only available for two model years, and it sold quite well. Dodge delivered nearly 80,000 units in 1971 and just under 49,000 examples in 1972. However, only a tiny fraction of these cars were Demon 340s (10,098 in 1971 and about 8,700 in 1972). They're far from rare by production numbers alone, but restored examples in excellent condition are hard to come by.
If you haven't seen one recently, this 1971 Demon 340 is one of those Mopars that has it all. It's finished in a high-impact color, it has the most potent mill available in a Duster, as well as a cool houndstooth interior.
The hue in question is called Butterscotch (or Bahama Yellow on Plymouth models) and was discontinued after the 1971 model year. It may not be the most desirable high-impact color, but it sure looks stunning on this Demon 340.
Speaking of the engine, the Dart became a slant-six and small-block V8 affair after the 1970 model year. In 1971, the compact came standard with an inline-six, while the optional 318-cubic-inch (5.2-liter) V8 provided up to 230 horsepower. The Demon 340 was powered by the range-topping 340-cubic-inch (5.6-liter) small-block V8, good for 275 horsepower.
It may not sound like a lot compared to what was available on the market in 1971, but we need to keep in mind that the Demon was lighter than a B-body Mopar, so a 340-equipped Dart was likely at least as fast as an intermediate fitted with a 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) big-block V8.
But you don't need to be a fan of compact cars to appreciate a fine classic. This Demon 340 is pretty much a concours-ready gem. Check it out in the video below.

When Volkswagen first brought the ID. Buzz to the US in 2024, its electric spin on the iconic hippie van had plenty of people talking.
While many were thrilled to see VW finally bring the electric minibus to the US, much of that excitement turned out to be nostalgia.
Starting at around $60,000, the ID. Buzz wasn’t exactly cheap. Plus, it only offered a range of up to 234 miles.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Volkswagen looks to change that with the next-generation ID. Buzz. During an interview with Auto Express at the 2026 Paris Auto Show this week, VW brand CEO Thomas Schäfer confirmed “they’re working on it,” when asked about the future of the electric minibus.
Schäfer admitted that the ID. Buzz “is in the wrong cost base,” confirming the new model will be more affordable.
2025 Volkswagen ID. Buzz (Source: Volkswagen)
It will also be based on the Group’s new Scalable Systems Platform (SSP), which VW promises will reduce costs and pave the way for software-defined vehicles.
While Volkswagen is revamping its lineup, using some of its most popular nameplates like the Polo and Tiguan, Schäfer said that the company will not reuse all of its iconic names. However, “the iconic stuff, you need to use, because the other new brands don’t have that. They have no history,” he added.
2025 Volkswagen ID. Buzz (Source: Volkswagen)
What will the new ID. Buzz look like? According to Volkswagen’s design boss, Andreas Mindt, it will require “lots of secret sauce,” a cornerstone of its new design language.
Although Mindt admitted that “people get tired” of retro-looking vehicles, as was the case with the new Beetle, the next-gen ID. Buzz will likely stay true to its timeless design with a modern twist.
“When you have a van, it doesn’t have too much character; one white van looks like the other white van. So what do you do to make it interesting?” Mindt asked.
2025 Volkswagen ID. Buzz (Source: Volkswagen)
The ID. Buzz is “one of the interesting ones,” he said, adding, “This I can promise you in the future: it will be interesting.”
Like the new ID. Polo and ID. Tiguan, the new electric minibus will feature Volkswagen’s updated interior design and infotainment system, including the return of physical buttons.
Based on VW’s new SSP platform, the next-generation ID. Buzz will offer improved driving range, faster charging, and more advanced software. The platform is designed to reduce costs, while Schäfer hinted it could also use lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries to enable lower prices.
Volkswagen ID. Tiguan interior (Source: Volkswagen)
Schäfer didn’t reveal any other details, including when the next-gen ID. Buzz will launch. The first SSP-based EV was initially set to arrive in 2026, but VW is now saying it will arrive “by the end of the decade.” The new ID. Buzz will likely launch shortly after.
In the meantime, Volkswagen recently delayed the return of the ID. Buzz in the US until the 2028 model year.
Volkswagen Group of America VP and chief communications officer, Jeannine Ginivan, told Electrek in December that the ID. Buzz would not receive a 2026 model year for the US. The company planned to move straight to the 2027 model.
Ginivan also confirmed with Electrek that “Volkswagen is not canceling the ID. Buzz for the US market.”
In the third quarter , Volkswagen sold just 432 ID. Buzz models in the US, down 82.5% from nearly 2,500 in Q3 2025.
